newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Jaguar car makes debut in the Philippines.
newsitem.headline: Jaguar car makes debut in the Philippines.

text.p: The British-made luxury car Jaguar was formally introduced in the Philippine market on Friday.

Steve Watts, Jaguar Cars Exports Ltd manager for the Far East, said in a statement the firm's entry into the Philippines is part of a long-term strategy to establish a broader presence in the Asian region.

Jaguar Cars Ltd, which is 100 percent-owned by Ford Motor Co of the U.S., had forged a joint venture and exclusive distributorship agreement with Frigate Holdings and Management Corp to locally market the Jaguar line through their corporate arm Jaguar Philippines Inc.
Frigate Holdings is an unlisted domestic company with diverse interests in food service, property development, and dealership of communications equipment.
Jaguar intends to market only 60 to 100 units yearly in the Philippines, said Wellington Soong, chairman of Frigate.

"We feel comfortable to start slowly. We just want to sell a number of vehicles relative to what we see is needed in the market," Wellington said, adding that the projected yearly sales of 100 units could double by the turn of the decade.

Jaguar would be competing with other luxury car models in the country such as the BMW, Mercedes Benz, Volvo, Audi and Alfa Romero. Sales of these luxury cars in the Philippines reached 1,523 units last year.
